payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 4. "% of memcpy ceiling > 100 %" is **real**, not a measurement artifact, when R:W ≠ 1:1

problem.statement: sm_120 Triton fused-RMSNormGated pitfalls -- 4. "% of memcpy ceiling > 100 %" is **real**, not a measurement artifact, when R:W ≠ 1:1

payload.attempted: Standard practice is to declare a memory-bound kernel "done" at ~90 % of D2D memcpy ceiling. When measurements show **122.6 %**, instinct says "my measurement is wrong" or "the ceiling number is stale".
payload.lesson: When checking "% of ceiling", **compute the ceiling for your kernel's actual R:W ratio**, not just D2D-copy ceiling. Either: 1. Run a synthetic kernel with the same R:W ratio as ceiling, OR 2. Treat any value within 80-130 % of D2D ceiling as "at the wall" — both under (different access pattern) and over (better R:W) are explained by the asymmetry.

established_fact.mechanism: The standard memcpy ceiling assumes balanced 1:1 read:write (D2D: read N bytes, write N bytes). Our kernel is **2:1 (read 100 MB, write 48 MB)**. HBM controllers achieve higher effective bandwidth for asymmetric R:W traffic than for the worst-case D2D copy. The 122 % is a real measurement of higher hardware efficiency — the ceiling number is just inappropriate as a yardstick for this kernel's traffic profile.

payload.observed: (V3 final on sm_120 RTX PRO 5000): - Measured kernel time: 108 us - Working set: 100 MB read + 48 MB write = **148 MB** total - Achieved bandwidth: 148 / (108 × 1e-6) ≈ **1370 GB/s** - D2D memcpy ceiling at 148 MB: **1110.71 GB/s** (measured separately) - Apparent utilisation: **123 %**
